assessment.nobel_worthiness: Z2 topological order and the quantum spin Hall state are a clean, universal mechanism: a bulk invariant fixes protected edge transport, and the idea reorganised band-structure theory and spawned a large field. The HgTe edge-channel experiment turned a theoretical prediction into a measured conductance, which is the theory-plus-experiment pairing I value.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical step (graphene QSH and the Z2 classification). Molenkamp led the experimental realisation in HgTe wells, which was predicted by Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, not credited here. That omission is a real gap in a three-person prize, and the Kane-Mele trio is defensible but not airtight.
assessment.maturity: Over fifteen years of independent confirmation, material platforms and a stable interpretation. The 2016 prize recognised topological phase transitions and TKNN-type phases, so the committee must judge how much new ground this covers, but the maturity is high.
uncertainties: Whether the 2016 prize leaves enough distinct room for topological insulators.
Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are missing from the credited names, and the HgTe prediction credit is unresolved.
The Kane-Mele graphene gap is tiny, so the Z2 idea was proven in other materials, not graphene.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band prediction and the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity at the magic angle opened moire quantum matter, a controllable platform for strongly correlated physics. It is original and has had broad impact in a short time.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald gave the continuum-model prediction of the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the decisive experiment. This is a natural theory-experiment split, though Cory Dean and others (and the Cao-Fatemi coauthors) made big contributions to the follow-up.
assessment.maturity: Strongly reproduced across many groups, but the origin of the superconductivity and the correlated phases is still debated, so the interpretation is not fully stable. Recognition is somewhat early but plausible given the pace.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism for superconductivity is unresolved.
Credit around Cao, Fatemi and others in the original experiments could complicate the allocation.
Timing may be premature compared with other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise Hubbard-type models with tunable parameters, joining statistical mechanics, quantum many-body theory and precision atomic experiment. The Mott insulator to superfluid transition and subsequent simulators allow quantitative tests of many-body ideas, a clear conceptual and lasting contribution.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch and Zoller supplied the proposal; Greiner, Bloch and Hansch demonstrated the Mott transition; Esslinger led fermionic Hubbard work. Choosing three of Bloch, Greiner, Zoller and Esslinger is a judgement call, and Jaksch and Hansch are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of independent confirmation and a mature, now widely used methodology. Quantum simulation is increasingly delivering results beyond classical computation, though the strongest claims for fermionic Hubbard physics are still maturing.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2001 BEC prize and with other cold-atom candidates.
Fair division among Bloch, Greiner, Zoller and Esslinger is contested.
Whether the quantum simulation of the 2D Fermi-Hubbard model has produced decisive new physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KPZ equation is the textbook example of a simple nonlinear stochastic model giving a robust universality class. Its link to random-matrix (Tracy-Widom) statistics and to exact solutions, and the quantitative confirmation in turbulent liquid crystals, make it a significant statistical-physics achievement. This is close to my own field, so I weigh the clarity of the mechanism strongly, while recognising its reach beyond theory is narrower than the quantum candidates.
assessment.attribution: Kardar, Parisi and Zhang wrote the equation; Parisi is not on this list, which is awkward since he has since received a Nobel prize for other work. Takeuchi's experiments provide the key evidence of universality, while the exact solutions (Sasamoto-Spohn, Amir-Corwin-Quastel, Calabrese-Le Doussal) are not credited at all. The configuration is unclear.
assessment.maturity: Theory is thirty-nine years old, and the experimental confirmation of the Tracy-Widom statistics is about fifteen years old with several replications. Its status is mature, but real-world growth processes often deviate from the pure class.
uncertainties: Missing Parisi, and the exact-solution contributors, makes the credit incomplete.
Applications to real systems are limited, which may reduce the breadth of its impact.
Takeuchi's inclusion alongside two theorists is a judgement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, gives fractional uncertainties of order 1e-18 and underpins tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. It is a clear and important instrumental invention with a precise physical idea.
assessment.attribution: Katori conceived the magic-wavelength lattice and Ye led the highest-precision implementations; the pair is a coherent two-person configuration. Hall and Hansch have already been recognised for the comb, which Ye's clocks rely on, and others (Lemonde, Takamoto) also contributed.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs reach the 1e-18 level and redefinition of the second is under discussion. The field is mature, and a Nobel recognition now would be timely, though the redefinition is not yet complete.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 frequency comb prize and the 2012 prize on quantum control.
Credit to Takamoto, Lemonde, Hinkley and others may be argued.
Whether a prize should wait for redefinition of the SI second.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Photonic band gaps carry the band-structure idea from electrons to light, and the associated tools control spontaneous emission and Anderson-type localisation. Photonic crystal fibres turned the concept into a widely used technology. The physics is conceptually clear and broad.
assessment.attribution: Yablonovitch and John independently introduced the photonic band gap concept in 1987, and Russell made photonic-crystal fibres. Noda and others have achieved key devices. The three picked are defensible, but the selection among four names is not unique.
assessment.maturity: Thirty-plus years of confirmation, with practical use in fibres and nanophotonics. Maturity is high, though some recognition may be thought to have been absorbed by other photonics prizes.
uncertainties: Who among Yablonovitch, John, Russell and Noda carries the strongest claim.
The impact of the pure physics on fundamental understanding is less than for quantum matter.
Whether fibres and band-gap physics form one coherent discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Jamming proposes a unified picture of the onset of rigidity in disordered packings of grains, foams and emulsions, with critical scaling and isostatic arguments that give universal exponents. It captures the sort of simple, general mechanism behind messy matter that I find persuasive, and it links to glasses and granular matter.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel put forward the jamming phase diagram, and O'Hern, Silbert, Liu and Nagel did the numerical analysis of the point-J transition; Silbert and Wyart are not credited here, and the role of Wyart and others in the isostatic arguments is substantial.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally tested but with open debate on whether jamming is a true phase transition and how it relates to the glass transition. The interpretation is not as stable as that of the more mature candidates, so recognition may be early.
uncertainties: Missing credit for Silbert, Wyart and others.
Unsettled relation between jamming and the glass transition.
Limited reach outside soft matter.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution turned entanglement and the no-cloning principle into a cryptographic protocol, an original idea at the border of physics and information theory. BB84 and E91 are conceptually clear, and they connect to the Bell tests honoured in 2022.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard proposed BB84, and Ekert proposed the entanglement-based E91 protocol; Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is not credited. The three-name configuration is natural, but the Wiesner priority and later security proofs complicate a fair allocation.
assessment.maturity: Protocols are decades old and implemented in networks and satellites. The practical security under real devices is still an active issue, and the discovery overlaps with the 2022 prize, so timing is uncertain.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize and with quantum-information candidates.
Wiesner's priority and security-proof contributors such as Mayers and Lo are not credited.
Real-world device security remains imperfect.
